strings.name: Andrew Bailey
strings.role: Bank of England Governor and Financial Stability Board Chair
strings.summary: Andrew Bailey is a British central banker and regulator. Trained in economic history, he joined the Bank of England in 1985 and became Chief Cashier, prudential supervisor and Financial Conduct Authority chief executive. Governor since 2020, he participates in monetary, supervisory and stability decisions and became FSB Chair in 2025. In 2026 he continued addressing energy-driven inflation, central-bank independence and AI-related risks.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads the Bank of England and contributes to UK monetary policy, bank supervision and financial stability.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Central-bank and regulatory experience
strings.highlights.h1.text: Worked across banking operations, resolution, prudential oversight and conduct regulation before leading the Bank from 2020.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended Wyggeston Boys School and Queens’ College, Cambridge; completed a history BA in 1981 and economic-history PhD studies in 1984, then researched at the LSE.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Committees and international coordination
strings.highlights.h2.text: Chairs central-bank policy committees and has chaired the FSB since 2025; interest-rate decisions are made by MPC votes.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Independence and technology speech
strings.timeline.t1.text: In Zurich, discussed central-bank independence and public accountability, AI’s productivity potential and valuation, cyber and trust risks.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became FSB Chair
strings.timeline.t2.text: Began a three-year term coordinating international financial regulation and stability while remaining Governor.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Started as Governor
strings.timeline.t3.text: Succeeded Carney for a term ending March 15, 2028, subsequently facing pandemic and inflation shocks.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Led the FCA
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became chief executive, overseeing financial conduct and consumer-protection regulation until 2020.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Prudential Regulation Deputy Governor
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became Deputy Governor and chief executive of the new PRA, responsible for institutions’ prudential supervision.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined the FSA
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined its prudential business unit while remaining a Bank executive director and later became the unit’s managing director.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Chief Cashier and banking operations
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became Chief Cashier and Executive Director for Banking, later also working on crisis resolution.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined the Bank of England
strings.timeline.t8.text: Moved from research at the LSE to the Bank, initially working on international capital markets.
